sentences.ko: 남의 카드를 훔치는 사람이면 이미 앞뒤 안 가리기로 한 거 아니야?
sentences.text: I think when somebody steals your credit card, they've kind of already thrown caution to the wind.

alts.text: Stealing someone's card? They're already past caring, right?
A person who steals a credit card has, in a sense, already abandoned all caution.

sentences.note: **thrown caution to the wind**는 '될 대로 되라, 앞뒤 안 가리고 저지르다'라는 뜻이에요. 충동구매나 무모한 결정을 두고 농담처럼 자주 써요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends

sentences.ko: 사실 좀 너무 편해서 탈인 것 같아.
sentences.text: In fact, I think I might be a little too comfortable.

alts.text: Actually, I believe I may be somewhat too comfortable.

sentences.note: **In fact**는 상대가 예상한 것보다 한발 더 나가는 말을 꺼낼 때 써요. **a little too**는 '좋긴 한데 지나쳐서 문제'라는 느낌을 부드럽게 전해요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 응, 그 사람이 카펫을 다 걷어내서 이제 소리가 다 들려.
sentences.text: Yeah, he took up the carpets and now you can hear everything.

alts.text: He ripped out the carpet, so I hear it all now.
He removed the carpets, and now every sound can be heard.

sentences.note: 바닥에 깔린 걸 걷어낼 때 **took up the carpets**처럼 take up을 써요. 윗집 소음 같은 층간소음 얘기할 때 그대로 쓸 수 있어요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 머릿속에 말 좀 걸러 주는 장치라도 있으면 얼마나 좋을까.
sentences.text: If only there was something in your head to control the things you say.

alts.text: Wish you had a filter, seriously.
It would be helpful if you had some way to control what you say.

sentences.note: **If only**로 시작하면 '~라면 얼마나 좋을까'라는 아쉬움이 담겨요. 생각 없이 말하는 친구한테 비꼬듯 할 때 딱 맞아요. 짧게 말하고 싶으면 **a filter**라고 해도 같은 뜻이에요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 8 | Friends

sentences.ko: 회사에서 좀 멀긴 한데, 뭐, 출퇴근하면서 이것저것 많이 할 수 있을 거야.
sentences.text: I mean, it's it's kind of far from work, but uh you know, I'll get so much done on the commute.

alts.text: Kinda far from work, but hey, I'll get loads done on the commute.
It is somewhat far from my workplace, but I will be able to accomplish a great deal during my commute.

sentences.note: **get so much done**은 '일을 많이 해치우다'라는 뜻으로, 바쁜 하루나 시간 활용을 말할 때 자주 써요. **on the commute**는 '출퇴근길에'라서 이사나 이직 얘기할 때 딱 맞아요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends

sentences.ko: 아니, 내가 지금 당장 애 낳고 결혼하고 싶다고 한 적은 없잖아.
sentences.text: I mean, I never said that I wanted to have babies and get married right now.

alts.text: Look, I never said I want kids and a wedding right now.
To be clear, I have never stated that I wished to have children and marry at this point.

sentences.note: **I never said that**은 상대가 내 말을 넘겨짚을 때 '그런 말 한 적 없어' 하고 바로잡는 말이에요. 앞의 **I mean**은 '아니 그러니까' 처럼 말을 고쳐 잡을 때 붙여요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends

sentences.ko: 이렇게 좋게 헤어져 본 건 처음이야.
sentences.text: I have never had such a healthy breakup.

alts.text: Wow, that's the healthiest breakup I've ever had.
This is the healthiest breakup I have ever experienced.

sentences.note: **I have never had such a** ~ 는 '이렇게 ~한 건 처음이야' 하고 놀라움을 말할 때 써요. **healthy breakup**은 싸우지 않고 서로 좋게 정리한 이별을 말해요.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 야, 너 이번 이별 털고 나면 우리 쇼핑 가자.
sentences.text: Oh, when you get over this breakup, we need to go shopping.

alts.text: Once you're over him, we're going shopping.
Once you have recovered from this breakup, we should go shopping together.

sentences.note: **get over**는 이별·실연·감기 같은 것을 '털어내다, 이겨내다'라는 뜻이에요. 힘들어하는 친구를 위로하면서 기운 내라고 할 때 자주 써요.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.text: I don't know who made you the boss.

alts.text: Since when are you the boss?
May I ask who put you in charge?

sentences.note: **who made you the boss**는 혼자 나서서 이래라저래라 하는 사람에게 '누가 너한테 그런 권한 줬어?' 하고 핀잔 줄 때 써요. 친구나 가족끼리 반쯤 농담으로 많이 해요.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends
